title: Travel, problems & emergencies
goal: Handle hotels and train journeys, report problems, ask for help in an emergency, and talk about conditions ('if… then').
intro: This unit gives you the language for when things go wrong — lost luggage, missed trains, accidents, illness — and the **conditional**, which in Tamil is a single suffix on the verb: **வந்தா** *vandā* 'if (someone) comes', **மழை பெஞ்சா** 'if it rains'. No separate word for 'if' is needed.

vocab.note: spoken: வந்து சேரு; past வந்து சேர்ந்தேன்
spoken: -ன்னா -nnā (attached to a noun or clause)

phrases.native: எனக்கு ஒரு ரூம் வேணும், ரெண்டு நாளைக்கு.
phrases.roman: enakku oru rūm vēṇum, reṇḍu nāḷaikku.
phrases.en: I need a room for two nights.
Which platform does the train arrive at?

phrases.native: எனக்கு வழி தெரியல. இந்த அட்ரஸ் எங்க இருக்கு?
phrases.roman: enakku vaḻi teriyala. inda aṭras enga irukku?
phrases.en: I don't know the way. Where is this address?
Don't be afraid, everything will be all right.

grammar.title: The conditional: -ஆ (written -ஆல்)
grammar.body:
To say **'if…'**, take the **past stem** of the verb and add **-ஆ** *-ā* (written **-ஆல்** *-āl*). It doesn't change for person, and there's no word for 'then':

வா → வந்தா *vandā* 'if (I/you/he…) come(s)'
போ → போனா *pōnā* 'if … go'
இரு → இருந்தா *irundā* 'if … is'
பார் → பாத்தா *pāttā* 'if … see'
சாப்பிடு → சாப்பிட்டா *sāppiṭṭā* 'if … eat'
மழை பெய் → மழை பெஞ்சா *penjā* 'if it rains'

The 'if' clause always comes **first**. For nouns and adjectives use **-ன்னா** *-nnā*: நீங்க தமிழ்னா 'if you are Tamil', காசு இல்லைன்னா 'if there's no money'.

examples.en: If it rains, we won't come.
If you have time, give me a call.
If you go straight, you'll reach the station.
If there's any problem, call me.
If I get a ticket, I'll leave tomorrow itself.

grammar.title: 'If not' and 'even if': -லைன்னா / -ஆட்டி, and -ஆலும்
grammar.body:
**Negative condition** 'if not / unless': infinitive + **-லைன்னா** *-lainnā* or the shorter **-ஆட்டி** *-āṭṭi*: வரலைன்னா / வராட்டி 'if (you) don't come', சாப்பிடலைன்னா 'if (you) don't eat'.

**'Even if / although'**: add **-உம்** to the conditional: வந்தாலும் *vandālum* 'even if (he) comes', மழை பெஞ்சாலும் 'even if it rains'. This also gives the connector **இருந்தாலும்** 'even so, however'.

examples.en: If we don't leave soon, the train will go.
If you don't come, I'll go alone.
Even if it rains, I'll come.
However much I searched, I couldn't find it.

dialogue.title: A missing bag at the station
dialogue.setting: Tom arrives at Egmore station and can't find his suitcase. He talks to a railway policeman.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: சார், கொஞ்சம் உதவி பண்ணுங்க. என் பெட்டியைக் காணோம்!
lines.roman: sār, konjam udavi paṇṇunga. en peṭṭiyaik kāṇōm!
lines.en: Sir, please help me. My suitcase is missing!

lines.speaker: Police
lines.en: Don't worry. Where did you put it?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: ட்ரெயின்ல சீட்டுக்குக் கீழ வச்சிருந்தேன். இறங்கும்போது பாத்தா இல்ல.
lines.roman: ṭreyinla sīṭṭukku kīḻa vacchirundēn. irangumbōdu pāttā illa.
lines.en: I'd put it under my seat on the train. When I looked as I got off, it wasn't there.

lines.speaker: Police
lines.native: பெட்டி என்ன கலர்? உள்ள என்ன இருக்கு?
lines.roman: peṭṭi enna kalar? uḷḷa enna irukku?
lines.en: What colour is the suitcase? What's inside?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: கருப்புப் பெட்டி. துணி, புத்தகம்… பாஸ்போர்ட்டும் அதுலதான் இருக்கு!
lines.roman: karuppup peṭṭi. tuṇi, puttagam… pāspōrṭṭum aduladān irukku!
lines.en: A black suitcase. Clothes, books… and my passport is in it too!

lines.speaker: Police
lines.native: சரி, இந்த ஃபார்ம்ல உங்க பேரு, ஃபோன் நம்பர், ஹோட்டல் அட்ரஸ் எழுதுங்க.
lines.roman: sari, inda fārmla unga pēru, fōn nambar, hōṭṭal aṭras eḻudunga.
lines.en: OK, write your name, phone number and hotel address on this form.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.en: If you find it, will you call me right away?

lines.speaker: Police
lines.en: Certainly. If it isn't found, come to the station tomorrow.

culture: India's emergency numbers: **112** (all emergencies), **100** (police), **108** (ambulance), **101** (fire). In an emergency, Tamils will gather quickly to help — shouting காப்பாத்துங்க! or simply ஐயோ! draws attention. On trains, the coach codes (S4, B2…) and berth numbers are essential; railway police (RPF) stations are found at all major stations.
